per_file.paper_title: Discovery of Van Hove Singularities: Electronic Fingerprints of 3Q Magnetic Order in a van der Waals Quantum Magnet

expected_output.experiment_description: Single-crystal 2H-TaS2 and Co0.32TaS2 were cleaved and measured by low-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) at the Advanced Light Source MAESTRO beamline using a hemispherical electron analyzer. The pristine 2H-TaS2 sample was measured at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 93 eV and linearly horizontal polarization. The Co0.32TaS2 sample was measured at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV and linearly horizontal polarization on the TaS2-terminated surface. Fermi-surface maps and energy–momentum cuts were acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction of the 2H-TaS2 Brillouin zone. Band dispersions were extracted by fitting Lorentzian peaks in momentum distribution curves and energy distribution curves. The comparison was used to quantify how Co intercalation modifies the TaS2-derived α and β bands and the spin-orbit-split momentum separation at the Fermi level.

alpha_band_minimum_shift_along_gamma0_k0.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the α-band minimum in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2 along the Γ0–K0 direction.

tas2_derived_band_bottom_shift_along_gam.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived band bottom in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2 along the Γ0–M0 direction.

tas2_derived_band_shift_at_m0_meV.description: Measured binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived band feature at M0 in Co0.32TaS2 relative to pristine 2H-TaS2.

spin_orbit_momentum_splitting_2h_tas2_in.description: Momentum splitting between the spin-orbit-split α and β bands at the Fermi level in pristine 2H-TaS2.

spin_orbit_momentum_splitting_co0_32tas2.description: Momentum splitting between the spin-orbit-split α and β bands at the Fermi level in Co0.32TaS2.

gamma_k_band_bottom_binding_energy_meV.description: Approximate binding energy of the shallow Co-derived γK electron-like band bottom near K in Co0.32TaS2.

gamma_m_band_top_binding_energy_meV.description: Approximate binding energy scale of the Co-derived γM hole-like feature near M in Co0.32TaS2.

expected_output.experiment_description: A Co-composition series of CoxTaS2 single crystals with x = 0.29, 0.31, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 was measured by ARPES at T = 7 K using photon energy hν = 79 eV and linearly horizontal polarization. Measurements were performed on TaS2-terminated surfaces. Energy–momentum spectra were acquired along the M0–Γ0–K0 high-symmetry direction, and energy distribution curves were taken at the M point. The α, β, γM, and γK band extrema were obtained from peak positions in fitted energy distribution curves, with γK extracted from spectra at the K point.

alpha_beta_band_downshift_x0_29_to_x0_36.description: Overall measured downward binding-energy shift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands when Co composition is increased from x = 0.29 to x = 0.36.

gamma_m_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: Small measured upward energy shift of the Co-derived γM band feature at x = 0.36 relative to its lower-composition trend.

gamma_k_band_upturn_at_x0_36_meV.description: Small measured upward energy shift of the Co-derived γK band feature at x = 0.36 relative to its lower-composition trend.

expected_output.experiment_description: A Co0.29TaS2 single crystal was measured by ARPES at T = 7 K using photon energy hν = 79 eV on a TaS2-terminated surface. The same cleaved surface was measured before and after successive in situ potassium depositions, with spectra acquired along the Γ0–K0 direction. Energy distribution curves at the M point were used to track the α, β, and γM band extrema as a function of potassium dosing.

gamma_m_band_shift_resolved_after_potass.description: Whether a resolvable shift of the Co-derived γM band was observed after potassium electron dosing of Co0.29TaS2.

alpha_beta_downshift_after_potassium_dos.description: Approximate downward shift of the TaS2-derived α and β bands after potassium dosing, described as comparable to the shift obtained by changing Co composition from x = 0.29 to x = 0.36.

expected_output.experiment_description: CoxTaS2 samples with Co compositions spanning x = 0.29 to 0.36 were measured by low-temperature ARPES at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV. Fermi-surface maps were acquired around the Co-derived γ pockets in the Brillouin zone of the Co triangular superlattice. The triangular γ Fermi pockets were extracted from the raw Fermi-surface intensity maps and from momentum distribution curves along the K–M direction, allowing the Fermi-pocket topology to be compared across Co composition.

gamma_fermi_pocket_size_trend_with_co_co.description: Observed evolution of the Co-derived triangular γ Fermi pockets over the measured Co-composition series.

fermi_surface_topology_change_across_xc.description: Observed qualitative change in the γ-pocket Fermi-surface topology across the composition range near the reported critical composition.

expected_output.experiment_description: CoxTaS2 samples with Co compositions x = 0.29, 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, and 0.36 were measured by ARPES at T = 7 K with photon energy hν = 79 eV. Energy–momentum spectra were acquired along the K–M–K′ direction of the Co triangular-superlattice Brillouin zone. Second-derivative images with respect to energy and energy distribution curve stacks were used to determine the near-Fermi γ-band dispersion near the M point. Detailed raw spectra and EDCs were analyzed for x = 0.29 and x = 0.36 to compare the dispersion curvature and van Hove singularity structure.

gamma_band_vhs_count_x0_29.description: Number of van Hove singularity features inferred from the measured γ-band dispersion near M along K–M–K′ for Co0.29TaS2.

per_file.paper_title: Device-independent quantum memory certification in two-point measurement experiments

expected_output.experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement quantum-memory test on a trapped-ion processor. A chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions was confined in a macroscopic linear Paul trap. The two outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion served only as a spacer to reduce optical cross-talk. Qubit manipulations used an individually addressed 729 nm quadrupole laser with linewidth below 1 Hz, incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis; single-ion addressing used a crossed acousto-optic-deflector setup. State readout used resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected onto an EMCCD camera. The two outer ions were initialized in a Bell state with a single Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit A′ was then measured at the first time point. A random variable X with alphabet {0,1,2,3} selected one of four Pauli measurements {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}; the binary first outcome was A. During this mid-circuit measurement, qubit E was spectroscopically decoupled by shelving it in unused D5/2 levels, followed by Doppler and polarization-gradient re-cooling. Qubit A was then re-prepared in a state depending only on A and not on X: the quantum-memory test used sigma_x eigenstates |+> and |-> as the two post-measurement states. A variable waiting time was inserted after the first measurement and before the two-qubit unitary; the displayed memory-decay experiment swept the wait time from 0 ms to 100 ms. Magnetic-field noise was mitigated with dynamical-decoupling echo pulses every 2.5 ms during the wait. The subsequent unitary consisted of a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP of the two qubit labels. The CNOT was implemented as R_C,0(pi/2) · R_T,pi(pi/2) · R_T,pi/4(pi) · MS_XX^{C,T}(pi/2) · R_T,pi/2(pi/2), where R_i,phi(theta) is a single-qubit equatorial rotation of qubit i by angle theta about phase phi, and MS_XX is a Mølmer-Sørensen XX interaction. The second-time binary measurement on qubit B was the observable (sigma_x+sigma_z)/sqrt(2). From the observed conditional probabilities Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), the classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was computed as the sum over b0,b1 of the infimum over x of the sum over a of Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x). The same probability data were also used to evaluate Pearl’s cross-talk witness Delta_Pr(AB|X), defined as the maximum over a of the sum over b of the supremum over x of Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x). Cross-talk was additionally addressed by estimating the average causal direct effect ACDE, the supremum over a,b,x,x′ of the absolute difference between Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) and Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b). The qubit-memory fidelity lower bound was inferred from Gamma_Pr(AB|X) using the paper’s device-independent qubit-memory bound.

temporal_correlation_gamma.description: Measured value of the two-point-measurement classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) for the optimized quantum-memory certification sequence with no added storage delay beyond the base sequence; classical memory models obey Gamma_Pr(AB|X) >= 1.

qubit_memory_fidelity_lower_bound_percen.description: Device-independent lower bound, in percent, on the fidelity of the implemented qubit memory channel to an ideal qubit memory channel inferred from the measured temporal correlations.

pearl_cross_talk_parameter.description: Measured Pearl-inequality parameter Delta_Pr(AB|X) obtained from the same optimized quantum-memory data; values above 1 would witness cross-talk influence.

average_causal_direct_effect.description: Measured average causal direct effect used to quantify direct cross-talk influence from the first measurement setting X to the second outcome B not mediated by A.

certified_quantum_memory_time_ms.description: Storage time over which the trapped-ion qubit memory was reported to be certified as quantum by the temporal-correlation protocol.

expected_output.experiment_description: Two-point-measurement experiment testing non-classical quantum causal relations with a partial-swap interaction on the same three-ion 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor. The outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E and were initialized in a Bell state using a single Mølmer-Sørensen gate; the middle ion acted as a spacer. Individual control used the addressed 729 nm laser at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis, and fluorescence readout used 397 nm light and an EMCCD camera. At the first time point, qubit A′ was measured with X in {0,1,2,3} selecting the four Pauli observables {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}, yielding binary outcome A. Qubit E was shelved during the mid-circuit measurement to suppress measurement back-action, and the ion chain was re-cooled afterward. The post-measurement qubit A was prepared in a sigma_y eigenstate depending only on A and not on X: |+i> for one binary outcome and |-i> for the other, according to the paper’s post-processing convention. The two-qubit interaction was the partial-swap gate U_PS(alpha)=cos(alpha/2) id + i sin(alpha/2) U_swap, where alpha is the controlled swap angle in radians, id is the two-qubit identity, and U_swap is the full two-qubit swap operator. The experiment swept alpha from 0 to pi. In the trapped-ion circuit, U_PS(alpha) was implemented as MS_ZZ(-alpha/2) · MS_YY(-alpha/2) · MS_XX(-alpha/2), with the Mølmer-Sørensen rotation angle controlled through laser intensity while keeping gate time fixed. The second-time measurement on qubit B was sigma_x. For each alpha, the same temporal-correlation classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was evaluated from Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), and violation of the classical causal bound was used to certify non-classical causal relations.

alpha_interval_with_observed_nonclassica.description: Swap-angle interval, in radians, over which the partial-swap two-point-measurement experiment exhibited violations of the classical causal inequality, thereby certifying non-classical causal relations.

expected_output.experiment_description: Noise and coherence characterization of the trapped-ion qubit memory used to model the decay of the two-point-measurement memory-certification signal. The same 40Ca+ trapped-ion processor was operated with qubit manipulation by the addressed 729 nm laser and readout by 397 nm fluorescence. Coherent magnetic-field noise at the 50 Hz mains frequency was actively compensated, while a remaining 100 Hz component was mitigated by dynamical decoupling. The experiment applied echo pulses at 2.5 ms intervals during variable waiting periods. Ramsey experiments were performed over a waiting-time sweep from 0 ms to 200 ms; the Ramsey contrast was measured as a function of waiting time and fitted with an exponential decay model to obtain the effective dephasing time T2 under the applied dynamical-decoupling sequence. The same echo pulse used in the memory sequence was also calibrated to estimate its average pulse fidelity.

effective_coherence_time_t2_ms.description: Effective dephasing time T2 of the trapped-ion qubit under the dynamical-decoupling sequence, obtained from an exponential fit to Ramsey-contrast decay.

single_echo_pulse_average_fidelity.description: Average fidelity of an individual echo pulse used in the dynamical-decoupling sequence for the memory-decay experiment.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Device-independent two-point-measurement quantum-memory test on a trapped-ion processor. A chain of three ground-state-cooled 40Ca+ ions was confined in a macroscopic linear Paul trap. The two outer ions encoded qubits A′ and E, while the middle ion served only as a spacer to reduce optical cross-talk. Qubit manipulations used an individually addressed 729 nm quadrupole laser with linewidth below 1 Hz, incident at 67.5 degrees to the trap axis; single-ion addressing used a crossed acousto-optic-deflector setup. State readout used resonant 397 nm fluorescence collected onto an EMCCD camera. The two outer ions were initialized in a Bell state with a single Mølmer-Sørensen entangling gate. Qubit A′ was then measured at the first time point. A random variable X with alphabet {0,1,2,3} selected one of four Pauli measurements {+sigma_x,+sigma_z,-sigma_x,-sigma_z}; the binary first outcome was A. During this mid-circuit measurement, qubit E was spectroscopically decoupled by shelving it in unused D5/2 levels, followed by Doppler and polarization-gradient re-cooling. Qubit A was then re-prepared in a state depending only on A and not on X: the quantum-memory test used sigma_x eigenstates |+> and |-> as the two post-measurement states. A variable waiting time was inserted after the first measurement and before the two-qubit unitary; the displayed memory-decay experiment swept the wait time from 0 ms to 100 ms. Magnetic-field noise was mitigated with dynamical-decoupling echo pulses every 2.5 ms during the wait. The subsequent unitary consisted of a CNOT gate followed by a virtual full SWAP of the two qubit labels. The CNOT was implemented as R_C,0(pi/2) · R_T,pi(pi/2) · R_T,pi/4(pi) · MS_XX^{C,T}(pi/2) · R_T,pi/2(pi/2), where R_i,phi(theta) is a single-qubit equatorial rotation of qubit i by angle theta about phase phi, and MS_XX is a Mølmer-Sørensen XX interaction. The second-time binary measurement on qubit B was the observable (sigma_x+sigma_z)/sqrt(2). From the observed conditional probabilities Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x), the classicality parameter Gamma_Pr(AB|X) was computed as the sum over b0,b1 of the infimum over x of the sum over a of Pr(A=a,B=b_a|X=x). The same probability data were also used to evaluate Pearl’s cross-talk witness Delta_Pr(AB|X), defined as the maximum over a of the sum over b of the supremum over x of Pr(A=a,B=b|X=x). Cross-talk was additionally addressed by estimating the average causal direct effect ACDE, the supremum over a,b,x,x′ of the absolute difference between Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x)=b) and Pr(B_do(A=a,X=x′)=b). The qubit-memory fidelity lower bound was inferred from Gamma_Pr(AB|X) using the paper’s device-independent qubit-memory bound.

per_file.paper_title: Voltage-controlled topological spin textures in the monolayer limit

expected_output.experiment_description: A monolayer CrI3 van der Waals device was fabricated by mechanically exfoliating CrI3 from bulk crystals in a nitrogen-filled glovebox and stacking it with hBN dielectric flakes and graphite/graphene contacts on a 285-nm SiO2/Si substrate. The representative device used a monolayer CrI3 sheet of approximately 0.7 nm thickness and an hBN dielectric layer of 9.8 nm thickness. Polar reflective magnetic circular dichroism (RMCD) was measured in a cryogen-free optical cryostat using a 633 nm laser with fixed power of approximately 3 µW focused onto the CrI3 region through a 50× objective. The reflected beam was detected with a photomultiplier tube and lock-in detection. For the zero-gate magnetic hysteresis measurement, the gate voltage was held at 0 V, the temperature was held at 10 K, and the out-of-plane magnetic field μ0H was swept between negative and positive values over the plotted range of approximately -0.16 T to +0.16 T. Temperature-dependent RMCD loops on the same monolayer device were also used to identify the disappearance of ferromagnetic order under zero gate bias.

zero_gate_coercive_field_T.description: Coercive magnetic field of the monolayer CrI3 ferromagnetic RMCD hysteresis loop at zero gate voltage and 10 K.

zero_gate_curie_temperature_K.description: Curie temperature of intrinsic monolayer CrI3 determined from temperature-dependent RMCD under zero gate voltage.

expected_output.experiment_description: Polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy was performed on monolayer CrI3 in the same magneto-optical cryogenic platform using a Witec Alpha 300R Plus low-wavenumber confocal Raman microscope coupled to a closed-cycle helium optical cryostat and superconducting magnet. The excitation laser wavelength was 633 nm, the laser intensity was approximately 0.3 mW, a 50× objective with numerical aperture 0.45 was used, the spectrometer grating was 1800 g/mm, and the typical integration time was 120 s. Raman spectra were collected in co-linear polarization geometry, denoted XX, and cross-polarized geometry, denoted XY, with the analyzer rotated before the collection fiber. Measurements were made at low temperature and as a function of temperature across the magnetic ordering regime to probe spin-lattice coupling in the monolayer.

a1g_phonon_frequency_cm_minus_1.description: Observed Raman frequency of the A1g phonon mode used to identify the monolayer CrI3 spin-lattice-coupled phonon response.

a1g_phonon_detected_polarization_channel.description: Polarization selection channels in which the A1g Raman phonon was detected in monolayer CrI3.

xy_a1g_intensity_enhancement_onset_tempe.description: Temperature below which the A1g Raman phonon intensity in the cross-polarized XY configuration showed a pronounced enhancement associated with spin-lattice coupling.

expected_output.experiment_description: A dual-gated monolayer CrI3 heterostructure consisting of graphene or graphite electrodes, hBN dielectric layers, and monolayer CrI3 was measured by polar RMCD at 10 K. The hBN dielectric thickness was 9.8 nm with dielectric constant 2.9, and the monolayer CrI3 thickness was approximately 0.7 nm. A 633 nm laser of approximately 3 µW was modulated by a photoelastic modulator at 50 kHz, reflected from the device through a non-polarizing beamsplitter, focused with a 50× objective of numerical aperture 0.55, and detected with a photomultiplier tube and lock-in amplifier. Gate voltage Vg was swept over the experimentally plotted range from 0 V to 16 V while the out-of-plane magnetic field μ0H was swept in both directions over the plotted interval of approximately -0.2 T to +0.2 T. The topological circular dichroism component RCDT was obtained by subtracting the conventional ferromagnetic reflective circular dichroism contribution RCDM from the total RMCD loop. RCDT peak positions were extracted by Gaussian fitting and tracked as a function of gate voltage for peaks associated with opposite signs of topological charge.

topological_phase_onset_gate_voltage_V.description: Gate voltage at which a nonzero RCDT signal first emerged, marking electrical switching from trivial ferromagnetic order to a topological magnetic phase in the monolayer CrI3 device.

anisotropy_sign_change_gate_voltage_V.description: Gate voltage near which the magnetic anisotropy changed from perpendicular to in-plane character, accompanied by an abrupt change in the RCDT response and the transition between the two skyrmion regimes.

positive_topological_charge_rcdt_peak_fi.description: Linear voltage-tuning slope of the magnetic field position of the RCDT peak associated with positive topological charge before the abrupt high-voltage shift.

negative_topological_charge_rcdt_peak_fi.description: Linear voltage-tuning slope of the magnetic field position of the RCDT peak associated with negative topological charge before the abrupt high-voltage shift.

expected_output.experiment_description: Temperature-dependent polar RMCD measurements were performed on the same monolayer CrI3 dual-gated heterostructure under a fixed applied gate voltage of 16 V. The RMCD setup used a 633 nm laser of approximately 3 µW, photoelastic modulation at 50 kHz, a 50× objective with numerical aperture 0.55, photomultiplier detection, and lock-in readout in the cryogenic magneto-optical system. At the fixed gate voltage, out-of-plane magnetic field μ0H was swept in both directions over approximately -0.2 T to +0.2 T while the sample temperature was varied across the plotted low-temperature range from 10 K to 27 K. Temperature-field RMCD phase diagrams were constructed for both magnetic-field sweep directions. RMCD peaks associated with maximal topological quasiparticle density were fit with Gaussian profiles, and their magnetic-field positions and half-peak widths were tracked versus temperature.

topological_to_in_plane_ferromagnetic_tr.description: Temperature at fixed 16 V gate bias where the topological magnetic phase disappeared into an in-plane ferromagnetic state.

in_plane_ferromagnetic_to_paramagnetic_t.description: Temperature at fixed 16 V gate bias where the in-plane ferromagnetic state transitioned to a paramagnetic state.

positive_topological_charge_peak_field_t.description: Magnitude of the linear decrease with temperature of the RMCD peak field corresponding to maximum density of positive-topological-charge quasiparticles at 16 V.

negative_topological_charge_peak_field_t.description: Magnitude of the linear decrease with temperature of the RMCD peak field corresponding to maximum density of negative-topological-charge quasiparticles at 16 V.

topological_transition_temperature_at_ab.description: Critical temperature of the topological magnetic phase at an out-of-plane magnetic field magnitude of 0.04 T under 16 V gate bias.

per_file.paper_title: Fundamental Tests of Quantum Geometric Bounds in Ionic and Covalent Insulators using Inelastic X-Ray Scattering

expected_output.experiment_description: Room-temperature inelastic x-ray scattering (IXS) was performed on covalently bonded diamond at Sector 9-ID of the Advanced Photon Source. The instrument used a liquid-nitrogen-cooled Si(111) primary monochromator and a Si(333) secondary channel-cut monochromator. Diamond spectra were collected with incident photon energy 8981.8 eV using a Ge(733) backscattering analyzer, giving 0.3 eV energy resolution. Momentum transfer was along q ∥ (1, -1, 0), with momentum resolution Δq ≈ 0.15 Å^-1; spectra were measured over approximately q = 0.32–4.55 Å^-1 and energy loss 0–100 eV by scanning incident energy. The quasi-elastic scattering contribution below about 3 eV was removed, and the electronic response was treated as vanishing below the diamond electronic gap used for the analysis. The measured photon-count spectra were converted to the density response χ''(q,ω) using the partial f-sum rule with cutoff Ω = 100 eV, including the four valence electrons per carbon atom, i.e. eight effective electrons per primitive unit cell, primitive lattice constant a = 2.52 Å, and negligible high-energy background screening ε∞ ≈ 1. For momenta where spectral weight persisted above 100 eV, the spectrum was extrapolated as I(q,ℏω>Ω)=c(q)Ω^3/(ℏω)^3, where c(q) is the average intensity between 94 and 100 eV. The four lowest-q points were excluded from the f-sum scaling fit. From the scaled χ''(q,ω), the Bures metric and quantum Fisher information density were obtained by frequency integration, and the dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) was computed from the resulting density-response quantum geometry. The static electronic dielectric function ε(q) was obtained by Kramers-Kronig evaluation of χ'(q,ω) at a small nonzero frequency inside the gap, and its large-q decay was fit over q ≥ 2.5 Å^-1 to ε(q)=1+exp(-α q), where α is the fitted electronic-response decay length.

static_dielectric_decay_length_alpha_A.description: Electronic-response decay length α obtained by fitting the experimentally extracted large-q static electronic dielectric function of diamond to ε(q)=1+exp(-α q).

dimensionless_quantum_weight_aK_at_q_1_5.description: Approximate dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) for diamond read from the plotted IXS-derived values at q ≈ 1.58 Å^-1.

dimensionless_quantum_weight_aK_at_q_2_5.description: Approximate dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) for diamond read from the plotted IXS-derived values at q ≈ 2.51 Å^-1.

dimensionless_quantum_weight_aK_at_q_3_7.description: Approximate dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) for diamond read from the plotted IXS-derived values at q ≈ 3.70 Å^-1.

dimensionless_quantum_weight_aK_at_q_4_5.description: Approximate dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) for diamond read from the plotted IXS-derived values at q ≈ 4.55 Å^-1.

expected_output.experiment_description: Room-temperature inelastic x-ray scattering (IXS) was performed on ionically bonded LiF at Sector 9-ID of the Advanced Photon Source. The instrument used a liquid-nitrogen-cooled Si(111) primary monochromator and a Si(333) secondary channel-cut monochromator. LiF spectra were collected with incident photon energy 6482.5 eV using a Ge(531) analyzer, giving 140 meV energy resolution. Momentum transfer was along q ∥ (1, 0, 0), with momentum resolution Δq ≈ 0.15 Å^-1; spectra were measured over approximately q = 0.32–3.70 Å^-1 and energy loss 0–100 eV by scanning incident energy. The quasi-elastic scattering contribution below about 3 eV was removed, and the electronic response was treated as vanishing below the LiF electronic gap used for the analysis. The measured photon-count spectra were converted to the density response χ''(q,ω) using the partial f-sum rule with cutoff Ω = 100 eV, including seven fluorine valence electrons plus two lithium valence electrons and one shallow lithium core electron, i.e. ten effective electrons per primitive unit cell, primitive lattice constant a = 2.84 Å, and negligible high-energy background screening ε∞ ≈ 1. For momenta where spectral weight persisted above 100 eV, the spectrum was extrapolated as I(q,ℏω>Ω)=c(q)Ω^3/(ℏω)^3, where c(q) is the average intensity between 94 and 100 eV. The three lowest-q points were excluded from the f-sum scaling fit. From the scaled χ''(q,ω), the Bures metric and quantum Fisher information density were obtained by frequency integration, and the dimensionless longitudinal quantum weight aK(q) was computed from the resulting density-response quantum geometry. The static electronic dielectric function ε(q) was obtained by Kramers-Kronig evaluation of χ'(q,ω) at a small nonzero frequency inside the gap, and its large-q decay was fit over q ≥ 2.5 Å^-1 to ε(q)=1+exp(-α q), where α is the fitted electronic-response decay length.

per_file.paper_title: First Experimental Demonstration of Beam Storage by Three-Dimensional Spiral Injection Scheme for Ultra-Compact Storage Rings

expected_output.experiment_description: An ultra-compact weak-focusing electron storage-ring demonstration beamline was operated to test three-dimensional spiral injection with and without a pulsed vertical kicker. A thermionic electron gun and chopper generated an electron bunch with momentum p = 297 keV/c, kinetic energy 80 keV, and pulse width 100 ns. The beam was transported through three rotatable quadrupole magnets, one bending magnet, and a pair of steering magnets, then injected into a solenoidal storage magnet at a pitch angle of 0.7 rad relative to the horizontal X-Y plane. The storage magnet consisted of main and auxiliary solenoidal coils adjusted with opposite polarities to provide a solenoidal field Bz = 8.77 mT on the storage midplane Z = 0 cm and a weak-focusing field with field index of order 10^-2 in the storage region. The storage-ring diameter was 22 cm and the electron revolution period was 4.7 ns. For the kicker-on condition, a 45 A, 140 ns pulsed current was applied to kicker coils of inductance 1.3 microhenry located at Z = ±15 cm, producing a radial magnetic field component Br < 0 along the injected trajectory to maintain downward steering into the weak-focusing region. For the kicker-off condition, the same beamline and magnet settings were used but no kicker pulse was applied. Beam storage was measured destructively with a vertically inserted plastic scintillating-fiber probe consisting of a 1 mm diameter, 20 cm long scintillating fiber read out by a photomultiplier tube. In the reported example, the probe tip was inserted to the storage midplane so that the fiber covered Z = 0 cm to Z = 20 cm. Waveforms from the scintillating-fiber probe, a bottom-mounted plastic scintillator beam-loss monitor, and the kicker current were averaged over 1000 shots. The noise level sigma_noise was defined as the rms voltage fluctuation in a pre-injection time window, and the operational storage criterion was a scintillating-fiber signal exceeding 5 sigma_noise for at least 1 microsecond after injection.

beam_storage_observed_with_kicker.description: Whether the scintillating-fiber probe signal satisfied the operational storage criterion when the 45 A, 140 ns kicker pulse was applied.

beam_storage_observed_without_kicker.description: Whether the scintillating-fiber probe signal satisfied the operational storage criterion when no kicker pulse was applied.

minimum_observed_storage_signal_duration.description: Lower bound on the duration for which the scintillating-fiber probe signal remained above the 5 sigma_noise threshold in the kicker-on measurement.

per_file.paper_title: Experimental characterization of the hierarchy of quantum correlations in top quark pairs

expected_output.experiment_description: CMS/LHC proton-proton collision data at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV were used to characterize the spin quantum state of top-quark--antiquark (t tbar) pairs in the lepton+jets decay channel. The input measurement was the doubly differential extraction of the t tbar spin density matrix in bins of invariant mass m(t tbar) and absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is the top-quark production angle in the t tbar center-of-mass frame relative to the proton beam direction. The analyzed phase-space bins were m(t tbar) in [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV, crossed with |cos(theta)| in [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. In each bin, the top and antitop spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_t_tbar = (1/4)(I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j), where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The spin analyzers were charged leptons and d-type quarks from top decays. This record uses the helicity basis, an event-dependent right-handed basis in the t tbar center-of-mass frame defined by unit vectors (khat, nhat, rhat), with khat along the top-quark flight direction, rhat=(phat - cos(theta) khat)/sin(theta), nhat=rhat cross khat, and the sign convention nhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) nhat and rhat -> sgn(cos(theta)) rhat. Because the helicity-basis orientation changes event by event, observables integrated over phase space characterize event-dependent, so-called fictitious, two-qubit spin states rather than a fixed-laboratory-axis spin state. From the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients, the following dimensionless quantum-information observables were computed per bin. The top-quark quantum discord D_t is measured in bits using log base 2 and is D_t = S(rho_tbar) - S(rho_t_tbar) + min_uhat[p_{+uhat} S(rho_{t,+uhat}) + p_{-uhat} S(rho_{t,-uhat})], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), rho_t=Tr_tbar(rho_t_tbar), rho_tbar=Tr_t(rho_t_tbar), Pi_{±uhat} are projectors for a spin measurement of the antitop along unit vector uhat, p_{±uhat}=Tr[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})], and rho_{t,±uhat}=Tr_tbar[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})]/p_{±uhat}; the minimization over uhat was numerical. The entanglement marker Delta_E is the Peres-Horodecki-based marker used for the same reconstructed spin state, with the separability boundary Delta_E=1 and Delta_E>1 denoting entanglement. The steering marker T is T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the steering threshold T=2*pi for the unpolarized two-qubit criterion. The Bell-correlation marker B is B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C; B>1 is the CHSH Bell-correlation threshold for the reconstructed state. The mixed-state magic observable M2_tilde is the second-stabilizer-Renyi-entropy-based quantity M2_tilde = -log2((1 + sum_i(P_i^4 + Pbar_i^4) + sum_ij C_ij^4)/(1 + sum_i(P_i^2 + Pbar_i^2) + sum_ij C_ij^2)). Central values were obtained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U^{-1}_{ij} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are measured polarization/spin-correlation coefficients, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1].

expected_output.experiment_description: CMS/LHC proton-proton collision data at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV were used to characterize the spin quantum state of top-quark--antiquark (t tbar) pairs in the lepton+jets decay channel. The input measurement was the doubly differential extraction of the t tbar spin density matrix in bins of invariant mass m(t tbar) and absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is the top-quark production angle in the t tbar center-of-mass frame relative to the proton beam direction. The analyzed phase-space bins were m(t tbar) in [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV, crossed with |cos(theta)| in [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. In each bin, the top and antitop spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_t_tbar = (1/4)(I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j), where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The spin analyzers were charged leptons and d-type quarks from top decays. This record uses the fixed beam basis, a right-handed coordinate system in the t tbar center-of-mass frame with axes (xhat,yhat,zhat), where xhat points toward the center of the LHC ring, yhat points vertically upward, and zhat is aligned with the proton beam direction phat. Because this basis has fixed spatial orientation rather than changing event by event, the reconstructed spin states are bona fide two-qubit spin quantum states for the chosen phase-space bins. From the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients, the following dimensionless quantum-information observables were computed per bin. The top-quark quantum discord D_t is measured in bits using log base 2 and is D_t = S(rho_tbar) - S(rho_t_tbar) + min_uhat[p_{+uhat} S(rho_{t,+uhat}) + p_{-uhat} S(rho_{t,-uhat})], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), rho_t=Tr_tbar(rho_t_tbar), rho_tbar=Tr_t(rho_t_tbar), Pi_{±uhat} are projectors for a spin measurement of the antitop along unit vector uhat, p_{±uhat}=Tr[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})], and rho_{t,±uhat}=Tr_tbar[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})]/p_{±uhat}; the minimization over uhat was numerical. The entanglement marker Delta_E is the Peres-Horodecki-based marker used for the same reconstructed spin state, with the separability boundary Delta_E=1 and Delta_E>1 denoting entanglement. The steering marker T is T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the steering threshold T=2*pi for the unpolarized two-qubit criterion. The Bell-correlation marker B is B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C; B>1 is the CHSH Bell-correlation threshold for the reconstructed state. The mixed-state magic observable M2_tilde is the second-stabilizer-Renyi-entropy-based quantity M2_tilde = -log2((1 + sum_i(P_i^4 + Pbar_i^4) + sum_ij C_ij^4)/(1 + sum_i(P_i^2 + Pbar_i^2) + sum_ij C_ij^2)). Central values were obtained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U^{-1}_{ij} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are measured polarization/spin-correlation coefficients, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1].

actual_output.experiment_description: CMS/LHC proton-proton collision data at center-of-mass energy sqrt(s)=13 TeV were used to characterize the spin quantum state of top-quark--antiquark (t tbar) pairs in the lepton+jets decay channel. The input measurement was the doubly differential extraction of the t tbar spin density matrix in bins of invariant mass m(t tbar) and absolute top production angle |cos(theta)|, where theta is the top-quark production angle in the t tbar center-of-mass frame relative to the proton beam direction. The analyzed phase-space bins were m(t tbar) in [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV, crossed with |cos(theta)| in [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. In each bin, the top and antitop spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_t_tbar = (1/4)(I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j), where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The spin analyzers were charged leptons and d-type quarks from top decays. This record uses the fixed beam basis, a right-handed coordinate system in the t tbar center-of-mass frame with axes (xhat,yhat,zhat), where xhat points toward the center of the LHC ring, yhat points vertically upward, and zhat is aligned with the proton beam direction phat. Because this basis has fixed spatial orientation rather than changing event by event, the reconstructed spin states are bona fide two-qubit spin quantum states for the chosen phase-space bins. From the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients, the following dimensionless quantum-information observables were computed per bin. The top-quark quantum discord D_t is measured in bits using log base 2 and is D_t = S(rho_tbar) - S(rho_t_tbar) + min_uhat[p_{+uhat} S(rho_{t,+uhat}) + p_{-uhat} S(rho_{t,-uhat})], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), rho_t=Tr_tbar(rho_t_tbar), rho_tbar=Tr_t(rho_t_tbar), Pi_{±uhat} are projectors for a spin measurement of the antitop along unit vector uhat, p_{±uhat}=Tr[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})], and rho_{t,±uhat}=Tr_tbar[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})]/p_{±uhat}; the minimization over uhat was numerical. The entanglement marker Delta_E is the Peres-Horodecki-based marker used for the same reconstructed spin state, with the separability boundary Delta_E=1 and Delta_E>1 denoting entanglement. The steering marker T is T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the steering threshold T=2*pi for the unpolarized two-qubit criterion. The Bell-correlation marker B is B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C; B>1 is the CHSH Bell-correlation threshold for the reconstructed state. The mixed-state magic observable M2_tilde is the second-stabilizer-Renyi-entropy-based quantity M2_tilde = -log2((1 + sum_i(P_i^4 + Pbar_i^4) + sum_ij C_ij^4)/(1 + sum_i(P_i^2 + Pbar_i^2) + sum_ij C_ij^2)). Central values were obtained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U^{-1}_{ij} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are measured polarization/spin-correlation coefficients, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1].

The analyzed phase-space bins were m(t tbar) in [300,400], [400,600], [600,800], and [800,13000] GeV, crossed with |cos(theta)| in [0.0,0.4], [0.4,0.7], and [0.7,1.0]. In each bin, the top and antitop spin state was reconstructed as a two-qubit density matrix rho_t_tbar = (1/4)(I2 tensor I2 + sum_i P_i sigma_i tensor I2 + sum_j Pbar_j I2 tensor sigma_j + sum_ij C_ij sigma_i tensor sigma_j), where I2 is the 2 by 2 identity, sigma_i are Pauli matrices, P_i and Pbar_j are the top and antitop polarization components, and C_ij is the spin-correlation matrix. The spin analyzers were charged leptons and d-type quarks from top decays. This record uses the fixed beam basis, a right-handed coordinate system in the t tbar center-of-mass frame with axes (xhat,yhat,zhat), where xhat points toward the center of the LHC ring, yhat points vertically upward, and zhat is aligned with the proton beam direction phat. Because this basis has fixed spatial orientation rather than changing event by event, the reconstructed spin states are bona fide two-qubit spin quantum states for the chosen phase-space bins. From the fitted polarization and spin-correlation coefficients, the following dimensionless quantum-information observables were computed per bin. The top-quark quantum discord D_t is measured in bits using log base 2 and is D_t = S(rho_tbar) - S(rho_t_tbar) + min_uhat[p_{+uhat} S(rho_{t,+uhat}) + p_{-uhat} S(rho_{t,-uhat})], where S(rho)=-Tr(rho log2 rho), rho_t=Tr_tbar(rho_t_tbar), rho_tbar=Tr_t(rho_t_tbar), Pi_{±uhat} are projectors for a spin measurement of the antitop along unit vector uhat, p_{±uhat}=Tr[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})], and rho_{t,±uhat}=Tr_tbar[(I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat}) rho_t_tbar (I2 tensor Pi_{±uhat})]/p_{±uhat}; the minimization over uhat was numerical. The entanglement marker Delta_E is the Peres-Horodecki-based marker used for the same reconstructed spin state, with the separability boundary Delta_E=1 and Delta_E>1 denoting entanglement. The steering marker T is T = integral d^2 uhat sqrt(uhat^T C^T C uhat), with the steering threshold T=2*pi for the unpolarized two-qubit criterion. The Bell-correlation marker B is B=m1+m2, where m1 and m2 are the two largest eigenvalues of C^T C; B>1 is the CHSH Bell-correlation threshold for the reconstructed state. The mixed-state magic observable M2_tilde is the second-stabilizer-Renyi-entropy-based quantity M2_tilde = -log2((1 + sum_i(P_i^4 + Pbar_i^4) + sum_ij C_ij^4)/(1 + sum_i(P_i^2 + Pbar_i^2) + sum_ij C_ij^2)). Central values were obtained by minimizing the negative log-likelihood -2 log L = sum_ij (o_i-x_i) U^{-1}_{ij} (o_j-x_j), where o_i are measured polarization/spin-correlation coefficients, U_ij is their covariance matrix, and x_i are fitted coefficients constrained to the physical interval [-1,1].

per_file.paper_title: Energy-resolved transport of ultracold atoms across the Anderson transition: theory and experiment

expected_output.experiment_description: An ultracold gas of 87Rb atoms was prepared as a Bose–Einstein-condensed cloud in the hyperfine state |1⟩ = |F = 2, mF = 1⟩ in a nearly isotropic optical trap with trap frequencies approximately 2π × (35, 25, 11) Hz. The cloud contained about 2 × 10^5 atoms, had temperature T ≃ 7 nK, condensate fraction fc ≃ 0.75, chemical potential μin/h ≃ 350 Hz, and Thomas–Fermi radii approximately (8, 12, 26) μm. A state-dependent three-dimensional blue-detuned optical speckle disorder was applied for atoms transferred into |2⟩ = |F = 1, mF = −1⟩. The speckle disorder had amplitude VR/h = 416 Hz, longitudinal correlation length σx = 1.45 μm, transverse correlation length σ⊥ = 0.30 μm, and geometric-mean correlation length σ = 0.50 μm, corresponding to correlation energy Eσ/h = 441 Hz. A radio-frequency pulse of duration trf ≃ 40 ms transferred approximately 5% of the atoms from |1⟩ to |2⟩, with the RF detuning setting the target energy Ef = ℏδrf. The resulting energy filter had rms width ΔE/h ≃ 14 Hz. Immediately after transfer, the optical trap was switched off and atoms remaining in |1⟩ were removed. The atoms in |2⟩ then evolved in the disordered potential while magnetically levitated against gravity; weak residual harmonic confinement remained in the horizontal x–y plane, so the analyzed expansion was along the vertical z direction. In-situ fluorescence imaging along x measured the column density ncol(y,z,t), which was integrated over y to obtain the one-dimensional density profile n1d(z,t). Density profiles were recorded for target energies spanning the Anderson transition, including Ef/h = 166, 246, and 366 Hz, at evolution times up to 5 s. The Anderson mobility edge was determined from the energy-resolved transport response of these density profiles across the disorder-induced transition.

per_file.paper_title: Analog-Digital Quantum Computing with Quantum Annealing Processors

expected_output.experiment_description: Single-qubit analog-digital control and readout were performed on a D-Wave 1178-qubit superconducting quantum annealing processor using 124 independent three-qubit source-target-detector systems. Each system consisted of one target flux qubit, one source qubit inductively coupled to the target for initialization, and one detector qubit inductively coupled to the target for readout. The processor used six independently controlled, 30 MHz low-pass-filtered annealing lines; the source, target, and detector qubits were placed on independently controlled lines. The programmable longitudinal fields were set to hi = 0. All qubits were initialized at anneal parameter s = 0. The source qubit was forward-annealed to s = 1 in a polarizing flux bias, the target qubit was brought to a fixed anneal point s* corresponding to target splitting Delta/h = 1.0 GHz, and the source qubit was rapidly quenched back to s = 0 to prepare the target. The target then evolved freely under H0 = -(Delta/2) sigma_z for an evolution time t. The detector qubit was rapidly quenched to s = 1 to measure the target magnetization in a basis set by detector flux bias. With zero source and detector flux bias, the protocol prepared the target approximately in |+> and measured in the sigma_x basis. For detector-basis calibration, the source flux bias was held at 0 microPhi0 and the detector flux bias was swept from -200 to +200 microPhi0. For source-basis calibration, the detector flux bias was held at -200 microPhi0 and the source flux bias was swept from -200 to +200 microPhi0. Magnetization was measured versus evolution time over approximately 0-30 ns, with fits performed over the post-transient time window reported in the supplement. The data were fit to a single-qubit Lindblad model with relaxation time T1, pure dephasing time Tphi, total dephasing time T2 = (1/(2 T1) + 1/Tphi)^(-1), source Bloch angles theta_s and phi_s, detector Bloch angles theta_d and phi_d, and precession angular frequency Delta/hbar.

single_qubit_median_relaxation_time_ns.description: Median single-qubit relaxation time extracted from large-detector-flux-bias Larmor-precession measurements across the 124 source-target-detector systems.

single_qubit_median_pure_dephasing_time_.description: Median single-qubit pure dephasing time extracted from zero-detector-flux-bias Larmor-precession measurements across the 124 source-target-detector systems.

expected_output.experiment_description: Two-qubit spin-exchange dynamics were measured on pairs of coupled target flux qubits on the same D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. Each target qubit had a dedicated source qubit for state preparation and a dedicated detector qubit for readout. The two target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point corresponding to Delta/h = 1.0 GHz with detunings deltaDelta_i = 0 and programmable longitudinal fields hi = 0. The effective weak-coupling Hamiltonian during target evolution was H_2Q = (J/4)(sigma_x1 sigma_x2 + sigma_y1 sigma_y2). Experiments included cases with programmed exchange couplings J/h = 0, 0.15 GHz, and 0.30 GHz, and the decoherence parameters were extracted from the J/h = 0.30 GHz data using the initial product state |10>. The source qubits applied a pi pulse to prepare one target in |1> while leaving the other in |0>; both targets were then evolved for variable time t and read out in the sigma_z basis using detector qubits. Magnetizations were averaged over 2000 shots per time point. The relaxation of <sigma_z1 sigma_z2> and the dephasing of oscillations in <sigma_z1> - <sigma_z2> were fit to an open-quantum-system model with independent relaxation and pure dephasing on the two target qubits. The reported statistics are medians over 62 different target-qubit pairs.

two_qubit_median_relaxation_time_ns.description: Median relaxation time extracted from two-qubit sigma_z-basis spin-exchange measurements.

two_qubit_median_pure_dephasing_time_ns.description: Median pure dephasing time extracted from decay of two-qubit spin-exchange oscillations.

two_qubit_single_qubit_coherence_time_T2.description: Single-qubit coherence time within the two-qubit open-system fit, derived from the extracted relaxation and pure-dephasing times.

expected_output.experiment_description: Single-excitation propagation in the transverse component of a clean periodic one-dimensional target-qubit chain was measured on the D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. The embedded chain contained L = 56 target flux qubits with periodic boundary conditions, each target qubit coupled to its own source and detector qubits. All target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point with transverse splitting Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h = -0.60 GHz, detunings deltaDelta_i = 0, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. One target qubit was initialized in the |+> state using a pi/2 source pulse while the other targets remained in the ground state. The target chain evolved under the fixed many-body Hamiltonian equivalent in the weak-coupling regime to an XY chain. The evolved state was measured in the sigma_x basis as a function of target-qubit position and evolution time, and the resulting space-time magnetization map was averaged over all possible initial-excitation positions and chain-reflection symmetry. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over position and time was used to determine the experimentally observed positive-frequency single-paramagnon dispersion peak. In the formula result, k denotes quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi, pi], Delta is the target transverse-field energy, J is the nearest-neighbor coupling energy, h is Planck's constant, and f(k) is the positive-frequency Fourier peak.

single_paramagnon_dispersion_frequency_G.description: Observed positive-frequency dispersion peak of the sigma_x magnetization Fourier spectrum for the clean periodic chain.

expected_output.experiment_description: Energy-excitation propagation in a clean periodic one-dimensional target-qubit chain was measured on the D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. The embedded chain contained L = 124 target flux qubits with periodic boundary conditions, each target qubit coupled to its own source and detector qubits. All target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point with transverse splitting Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h = -0.60 GHz, detunings deltaDelta_i = 0, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. One target qubit was initialized in the |1> state using a pi source pulse while the other targets remained in the ground state. The target chain evolved under the fixed many-body Hamiltonian equivalent in the weak-coupling regime to an XY chain. The evolved state was measured in the sigma_z basis as a function of target-qubit position and evolution time, and the excitation probability was computed as (1 - <sigma_z>)/2. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over position and time was used to determine the experimental continuum peak. In the formula result, k denotes quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi, pi], J is the nearest-neighbor coupling energy, h is Planck's constant, and f(k) is the Fourier peak frequency branch.

sigma_z_excitation_density_fourier_peak_.description: Observed Fourier-spectrum peak of the sigma_z-basis excitation-density propagation signal in the clean periodic chain.

expected_output.experiment_description: Anderson localization was probed in a disordered periodic one-dimensional target-qubit chain on the D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. The embedded chain contained L = 124 target flux qubits with periodic boundary conditions, each target qubit coupled to its own source and detector qubits. All target qubits were held near a fixed anneal point with quantizing transverse field Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor coupling J/h = 0.20 GHz, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. Odd-indexed target qubits were initialized in |1> using pi source pulses while even-indexed qubits were left in |0>, giving an initial staggered configuration |1010...>. Disorder was introduced through per-qubit detunings deltaDelta_i drawn uniformly from [-J W/2, J W/2], where W is the dimensionless disorder strength; programmed couplings were compensated for the unwanted coupling shifts caused by anneal-offset detunings. The chain was evolved for variable time and read out in the sigma_z basis. The imbalance was computed as I(t) = (p_odd(t) - p_even(t))/(p_odd(t) + p_even(t)), where p_odd = (1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2} [1 - <sigma_z_{2i-1}>] and p_even = (1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2} [1 - <sigma_z_{2i}>]. Experimental curves were averaged over 20 disorder realizations. The time-averaged imbalance I_tilde was defined as the average of I(t) over normalized times J t/hbar from 6*pi to 8*pi, where hbar is the reduced Planck constant.

small_disorder_time_averaged_imbalance_s.description: Empirical small-disorder scaling of the time-averaged imbalance in the Anderson-localized chain.

All target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point with transverse splitting Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h = -0.60 GHz, detunings deltaDelta_i = 0, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. One target qubit was initialized in the |1> state using a pi source pulse while the other targets remained in the ground state. The target chain evolved under the fixed many-body Hamiltonian equivalent in the weak-coupling regime to an XY chain. The evolved state was measured in the sigma_z basis as a function of target-qubit position and evolution time, and the excitation probability was computed as (1 - <sigma_z>)/2. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over position and time was used to determine the experimental continuum peak. In the formula result, k denotes quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi, pi], J is the nearest-neighbor coupling energy, h is Planck's constant, and f(k) is the Fourier peak frequency branch.

sigma_z_excitation_density_fourier_peak_.description: Observed Fourier-spectrum peak of the sigma_z-basis excitation-density propagation signal in the clean periodic chain.

actual_output.experiment_description: Anderson localization was probed in a disordered periodic one-dimensional target-qubit chain on the D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. The embedded chain contained L = 124 target flux qubits with periodic boundary conditions, each target qubit coupled to its own source and detector qubits. All target qubits were held near a fixed anneal point with quantizing transverse field Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor coupling J/h = 0.20 GHz, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. Odd-indexed target qubits were initialized in |1> using pi source pulses while even-indexed qubits were left in |0>, giving an initial staggered configuration |1010...>. Disorder was introduced through per-qubit detunings deltaDelta_i drawn uniformly from [-J W/2, J W/2], where W is the dimensionless disorder strength; programmed couplings were compensated for the unwanted coupling shifts caused by anneal-offset detunings. The chain was evolved for variable time and read out in the sigma_z basis. The imbalance was computed as I(t) = (p_odd(t) - p_even(t))/(p_odd(t) + p_even(t)), where p_odd = (1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2} [1 - <sigma_z_{2i-1}>] and p_even = (1/L) sum_{i=1}^{L/2} [1 - <sigma_z_{2i}>]. Experimental curves were averaged over 20 disorder realizations. The time-averaged imbalance I_tilde was defined as the average of I(t) over normalized times J t/hbar from 6*pi to 8*pi, where hbar is the reduced Planck constant.

small_disorder_time_averaged_imbalance_s.description: Empirical small-disorder scaling of the time-averaged imbalance in the Anderson-localized chain.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Single-qubit analog-digital control and readout were performed on a D-Wave 1178-qubit superconducting quantum annealing processor using 124 independent three-qubit source-target-detector systems. Each system consisted of one target flux qubit, one source qubit inductively coupled to the target for initialization, and one detector qubit inductively coupled to the target for readout. The processor used six independently controlled, 30 MHz low-pass-filtered annealing lines; the source, target, and detector qubits were placed on independently controlled lines. The programmable longitudinal fields were set to hi = 0. All qubits were initialized at anneal parameter s = 0. The source qubit was forward-annealed to s = 1 in a polarizing flux bias, the target qubit was brought to a fixed anneal point s* corresponding to target splitting Delta/h = 1.0 GHz, and the source qubit was rapidly quenched back to s = 0 to prepare the target. The target then evolved freely under H0 = -(Delta/2) sigma_z for an evolution time t. The detector qubit was rapidly quenched to s = 1 to measure the target magnetization in a basis set by detector flux bias. With zero source and detector flux bias, the protocol prepared the target approximately in |+> and measured in the sigma_x basis. For detector-basis calibration, the source flux bias was held at 0 microPhi0 and the detector flux bias was swept from -200 to +200 microPhi0. For source-basis calibration, the detector flux bias was held at -200 microPhi0 and the source flux bias was swept from -200 to +200 microPhi0. Magnetization was measured versus evolution time over approximately 0-30 ns, with fits performed over the post-transient time window reported in the supplement. The data were fit to a single-qubit Lindblad model with relaxation time T1, pure dephasing time Tphi, total dephasing time T2 = (1/(2 T1) + 1/Tphi)^(-1), source Bloch angles theta_s and phi_s, detector Bloch angles theta_d and phi_d, and precession angular frequency Delta/hbar.

result_rows.description: Median single-qubit relaxation time extracted from large-detector-flux-bias Larmor-precession measurements across the 124 source-target-detector systems.
Median single-qubit pure dephasing time extracted from zero-detector-flux-bias Larmor-precession measurements across the 124 source-target-detector systems.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Two-qubit spin-exchange dynamics were measured on pairs of coupled target flux qubits on the same D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. Each target qubit had a dedicated source qubit for state preparation and a dedicated detector qubit for readout. The two target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point corresponding to Delta/h = 1.0 GHz with detunings deltaDelta_i = 0 and programmable longitudinal fields hi = 0. The effective weak-coupling Hamiltonian during target evolution was H_2Q = (J/4)(sigma_x1 sigma_x2 + sigma_y1 sigma_y2). Experiments included cases with programmed exchange couplings J/h = 0, 0.15 GHz, and 0.30 GHz, and the decoherence parameters were extracted from the J/h = 0.30 GHz data using the initial product state |10>. The source qubits applied a pi pulse to prepare one target in |1> while leaving the other in |0>; both targets were then evolved for variable time t and read out in the sigma_z basis using detector qubits. Magnetizations were averaged over 2000 shots per time point. The relaxation of <sigma_z1 sigma_z2> and the dephasing of oscillations in <sigma_z1> - <sigma_z2> were fit to an open-quantum-system model with independent relaxation and pure dephasing on the two target qubits. The reported statistics are medians over 62 different target-qubit pairs.

result_rows.description: Median relaxation time extracted from two-qubit sigma_z-basis spin-exchange measurements.
Median pure dephasing time extracted from decay of two-qubit spin-exchange oscillations.
Single-qubit coherence time within the two-qubit open-system fit, derived from the extracted relaxation and pure-dephasing times.

report_experiments.experiment_description: Single-excitation propagation in the transverse component of a clean periodic one-dimensional target-qubit chain was measured on the D-Wave superconducting quantum annealing processor. The embedded chain contained L = 56 target flux qubits with periodic boundary conditions, each target qubit coupled to its own source and detector qubits. All target qubits were held at a fixed anneal point with transverse splitting Delta/h = 2.0 GHz, nearest-neighbor exchange coupling J/h = -0.60 GHz, detunings deltaDelta_i = 0, and longitudinal fields hi = 0. One target qubit was initialized in the |+> state using a pi/2 source pulse while the other targets remained in the ground state. The target chain evolved under the fixed many-body Hamiltonian equivalent in the weak-coupling regime to an XY chain. The evolved state was measured in the sigma_x basis as a function of target-qubit position and evolution time, and the resulting space-time magnetization map was averaged over all possible initial-excitation positions and chain-reflection symmetry. A two-dimensional Fourier transform over position and time was used to determine the experimentally observed positive-frequency single-paramagnon dispersion peak. In the formula result, k denotes quasimomentum in the first Brillouin zone [-pi, pi], Delta is the target transverse-field energy, J is the nearest-neighbor coupling energy, h is Planck's constant, and f(k) is the positive-frequency Fourier peak.

result_rows.description: Observed positive-frequency dispersion peak of the sigma_x magnetization Fourier spectrum for the clean periodic chain.
result_rows.status_title: The reference simplifies to f(k)=sqrt(Delta^2+2Delta J cos(k)+J^2)/h (since (Delta+J cos k)^2+J^2 sin^2 k=Delta^2+2Delta J cos k+J^2). The predicted expression corresponds to sqrt(Delta^2+4Delta J cos(k)+4J^2 cos^2 k)/h, which has different coefficients and different dependence on k (J^2 term is multiplied by cos^2(k) and the cross term has 4 instead of 2).

per_file.paper_title: Strong-field ionization of atoms with bright squeezed vacuum light

expected_output.experiment_description: Strong-field ionization of xenon atoms was performed with BSV driving pulses in a Cold Target Recoil Ion Momentum Spectroscopy (COLTRIMS) apparatus. The BSV pulses were centered near 1600 nm and generated by the double-BBO type-I SPDC source pumped by 800 nm, 25 fs, 3 kHz Ti:sapphire pulses. The BSV pulses were focused into a pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet inside a high-vacuum chamber maintained at 5 × 10^-11 mbar using a concave mirror with 75 mm focal length. The xenon backing pressure was 0.7 atm. Electrons produced by ionization were extracted and guided by calibrated electric and magnetic fields to a microchannel-plate detector with delay-line readout, giving time- and position-resolved single-electron detection and reconstruction of three-dimensional electron momenta. Millions of events were accumulated for each condition. The BSV average pulse energies were swept over 3.3, 5.0, 8.3, and 10 µJ, corresponding to average peak intensities of 0.53, 0.80, 1.33, and 1.60 × 10^14 W/cm^2. The measured photoelectron momentum distributions were analyzed in the px–pz projection for the presence or absence of above-threshold-ionization intercycle peaks/rings and intracycle spider-like holographic fringes from indirect–forward-scattered electron trajectory interference.

ati_peaks_suppressed_for_all_bsv_energie.description: Whether above-threshold-ionization peak/ring features were suppressed in the measured BSV-driven xenon photoelectron momentum distributions throughout the tested BSV pulse-energy range.

spider_like_holographic_fringes_present_.description: Whether spider-like holographic interference fringes were observed in the measured BSV-driven xenon photoelectron momentum distributions throughout the tested BSV pulse-energy range.

expected_output.experiment_description: A direct comparison of xenon strong-field ionization by bright squeezed vacuum and by coherent-state mid-infrared light was carried out in the same COLTRIMS geometry. For the BSV case, 1600 nm BSV pulses with 10 µJ average pulse energy and 1.60 × 10^14 W/cm^2 average peak intensity were focused into the pulsed supersonic xenon gas jet. For the coherent-state case, the BSV beam was replaced by 1600 nm coherent-state pulses from an optical parametric amplifier pumped by the same Ti:sapphire laser system; these pulses passed through the same optical path and were focused onto the xenon target with the same geometry at 1.0 × 10^14 W/cm^2 intensity. The chamber pressure, xenon backing pressure, electron extraction fields, and MCP delay-line detection scheme were the same as for the BSV ionization measurements. Three-dimensional photoelectron momenta were reconstructed event-by-event and plotted as pr versus pz, where pr is the radial transverse momentum defined by pr = sqrt(px^2 + py^2), with px and py the two momentum components transverse to the laser polarization and pz the momentum along the laser polarization. The distributions were analyzed for above-threshold-ionization rings, carpet-like interference patterns, and spider-like holographic fringes.

bsv_10_uJ_spider_like_holographic_fringe.description: Presence of spider-like holographic interference fringes in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

bsv_10_uJ_ati_rings_observed.description: Presence of pronounced above-threshold-ionization rings in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

bsv_10_uJ_carpet_like_interference_obser.description: Presence of carpet-like interference structures in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by 10 µJ BSV pulses.

coherent_1600_nm_ati_rings_observed.description: Presence of pronounced above-threshold-ionization rings in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by the 1600 nm coherent-state driving field.

coherent_1600_nm_carpet_like_interferenc.description: Presence of carpet-like interference structures in the measured pr–pz photoelectron momentum distribution for xenon ionized by the 1600 nm coherent-state driving field.

coherent_1600_nm_second_order_correlatio.description: Measured zero-delay second-order intensity correlation of the coherent-state 1600 nm driving light used for the xenon ionization comparison.

per_file.paper_title: Attosecond quantum spectroscopy with entangled photon pairs

expected_output.experiment_description: Bright squeezed-vacuum light was generated by high-gain type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion using near-infrared pump pulses from a commercial Yb:YAG femtosecond fiber laser. The pump pulses had wavelength 1030 nm, pulse energy 2 mJ, pulse duration 140 fs, and tunable repetition rate in the range 1 Hz to 10 kHz. A portion of the pump beam was reduced in diameter and sent through two tandem 3-mm-thick BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm to select the lowest-divergence spatial mode. A band-pass filter centered at 2050 nm with 100 nm FWHM isolated the degenerate spectral Schmidt mode, producing filtered bright squeezed vacuum centered near 2060 nm with average pulse energy about 0.8 microjoule. More than 10000 single-shot spectra of the filtered field were recorded with a near-infrared spectrometer, and the photon-number distribution was used to calculate the time-domain second-order correlation at zero delay using g2 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the detected photon number in one pulse and angle brackets denote averaging over shots.

filtered_bsv_zero_delay_second_order_cor.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the spectrally filtered, near-single-mode bright squeezed-vacuum driving field.

expected_output.experiment_description: High-harmonic generation was driven in a 200-micrometer-thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal using the spectrally filtered bright squeezed-vacuum field generated by type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion in two tandem 3-mm BBO crystals pumped by 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG laser pulses. The filtered bright squeezed-vacuum drive was centered near 2060 nm, isolated with a 2050 nm center-wavelength, 100 nm FWHM band-pass filter, and focused by an off-axis parabolic mirror of focal length 25.4 mm into the lithium niobate crystal. The drive intensity at the crystal approached 1.2 TW/cm^2, and the laser polarization was aligned along the lithium niobate Gamma-Z axis. Generated harmonics were collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror and recorded shot-by-shot with a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer equipped with a PIX-100B high-efficiency detector. Harmonic orders from the second through the tenth were analyzed. For each selected harmonic order, single-shot photon-number distributions were obtained and the zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation was calculated as g2 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the detected photon number in the selected harmonic order and angle brackets denote averaging over laser shots.

fourth_harmonic_zero_delay_second_order_.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the fourth harmonic emitted from lithium niobate under filtered bright squeezed-vacuum driving.

fifth_harmonic_zero_delay_second_order_c.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the fifth harmonic emitted from lithium niobate under filtered bright squeezed-vacuum driving.

eighth_harmonic_zero_delay_second_order_.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the eighth harmonic emitted from lithium niobate under filtered bright squeezed-vacuum driving.

tenth_harmonic_zero_delay_second_order_c.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the tenth harmonic emitted from lithium niobate under filtered bright squeezed-vacuum driving.

harmonic_order_of_maximum_measured_bunch.description: Harmonic order at which the measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation reached its maximum within the analyzed second-through-tenth harmonic range.

expected_output.experiment_description: Multimode bright squeezed-vacuum light was generated by high-gain type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion using 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs pulses from a Yb:YAG femtosecond fiber laser with repetition rate tunable from 1 Hz to 10 kHz. The pump beam was sent through two tandem 3-mm-thick BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm. No spectral band-pass filter was placed after the BBO crystals, so the output retained several lower-order spectral Schmidt modes, including degenerate and non-degenerate modes. The unfiltered multimode bright squeezed-vacuum field was characterized by recording single-shot spectra with a near-infrared spectrometer and by analyzing the shot-to-shot photon-number distribution. The zero-delay second-order correlation was computed as g2 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the photon number in one pulse and angle brackets denote averaging over shots.

multimode_bsv_zero_delay_second_order_co.description: Measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the unfiltered multimode bright squeezed-vacuum driving field.

expected_output.experiment_description: High-harmonic generation was driven in a 200-micrometer-thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal using unfiltered multimode bright squeezed-vacuum light containing lower-order spectral Schmidt modes and non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair components. The bright squeezed-vacuum source was produced by type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion in two tandem 3-mm BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm and pumped by 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG laser pulses. Without spectral filtering, the average single-pulse energy of the multimode field reached about 2 microjoules. The quantum light was focused into the lithium niobate crystal by an off-axis parabolic mirror with focal length 25.4 mm, with polarization aligned along the crystal Gamma-Z axis. Harmonic emission was collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror and recorded shot-by-shot using a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer with a PIX-100B detector. For the third harmonic, wavelength-resolved single-shot photon-number data over the harmonic spectral range were used to calculate g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>), where lambda and lambda' are wavelength bins, N(lambda) is the detected photon number in a wavelength bin, and angle brackets denote averaging over shots. The normalized correlation map was calculated as Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda,lambda)g2(lambda',lambda')].

third_harmonic_wavelength_resolved_g2_pe.description: Number of distinct peaks observed in the wavelength-resolved zero-delay second-order correlation spectrum of the third harmonic under multimode bright squeezed-vacuum driving.

third_harmonic_off_diagonal_spectral_cor.description: Whether the measured wavelength-resolved second-order cross-correlation and normalized correlation maps of the third harmonic showed symmetric off-diagonal correlation lobes between spectrally distinct harmonic components.

expected_output.experiment_description: Second- and fourth-harmonic emission from a 200-micrometer-thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal was measured under unfiltered multimode bright squeezed-vacuum driving. The driving field was generated by type-I spontaneous parametric down-conversion in two tandem 3-mm-thick BBO crystals pumped by 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG laser pulses, with no spectral band-pass filter after the crystals so that non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair modes remained present. The multimode bright squeezed-vacuum beam was focused into the lithium niobate crystal by a 25.4 mm focal-length off-axis parabolic mirror, with polarization along the Gamma-Z axis. Harmonic spectra were recorded shot-by-shot with a grating spectrometer and CCD detector. For the second harmonic, normalized wavelength-resolved correlation maps Gamma(lambda,lambda') were evaluated over approximately 950 to 1100 nm; for the fourth harmonic, the same analysis was performed over approximately 450 to 550 nm. Here lambda and lambda' are harmonic wavelength bins, Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda,lambda)g2(lambda',lambda')], and g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>).
